questions.title: Sort Words by Length Then Alphabetically
questions.description:
You are given a single line containing space-separated lowercase words.

Print the same words, space-separated, on **one line**, sorted by:

1. **Word length**, increasing first.
2. For words of the **same length**, **alphabetical order** (lexicographically ascending) as the tie-break.

If a word appears more than once in the input, it must appear the same number of times in the output (duplicates are kept, not removed).

### Input
A single line of space-separated lowercase words.
```
banana apple kiwi fig
```

### Output
The words on one line, separated by single spaces, sorted as described above.
```
fig kiwi apple banana
```

`fig` (3 letters) comes first, then `kiwi` (4), then `apple` (5), then `banana` (6) — all different lengths here, so length alone decides the order.

### Tie-break example
For input `pear plum kiwi lime` (all four words are 4 letters long), the length comparison is a tie for every pair, so the output falls back to plain alphabetical order:
```
kiwi lime pear plum
```
